comments.body: 2026-10-07: hidden panes landed as a daemon tab flagged hidden that no window claims, and pane hide / show / quiet already work with no window. What is left here for pane new: with no window, pane new --hidden can make the pane in a hidden tab on the daemon, which a window shows later from its Hidden list.
comments.author: Alexander Terp

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
amterp, 2026-10-07: "let's say that the main daemon ... is on machine A, and then ... machine B ... has its own daemon ... if machine A is shut down, are agents running on machine B ... able to still run muster commands through its own daemon? Or are they gonna have issues because the main daemon on machine A is down? That's one thing to just kind of check and potentially fix."

What the docs say today (`muster docs overview` "With no window", `muster docs limits`): B's agents keep running, since B's daemon owns their PTYs. `muster msg` asks B's daemon and works for groups kept on B. `window`, `pane read`, `pane send`, `pane wait` and `pane compact` fall back to B's daemon, but while A sleeps with its forward open each command first pays a 2 s probe. Everything else - `pane new`, `pane rename`, `pane close`, anything about tabs - needs a window and exits 3 after 10 s. So an orchestrating agent on B cannot spawn a worker while the laptop is gone, and a group kept on A (one with @human in it) is out of reach.

To do: check each of those on a real devenv with the laptop's window quit, asleep and gone; then fix what can be fixed. `pane rename` and `pane close` are the daemon's to do already. `pane new` with no window needs somewhere for the pane to live, which is the hidden-pane card's question (a_2die7jO4X) too.
title: 🔌 With the laptop gone, a devenv agent cannot make, rename or close panes
